scope: Dated public events and attributable public statements. Events may be evidenced by official records and reported observation; the separate Myth vs Reality claim register admits only statements made in interviews, public speeches, press conferences and press interactions. Not exhaustive.

events.title: Remarks in Supreme Court hearing
events.assessment: Reporting traces the movement’s origin to comments attributed to Chief Justice Surya Kant. The context and his subsequent clarification matter; protest slogans should not substitute for the full exchange.

events.title: Satirical CJP movement launches online
events.assessment: Abhijeet Dipke’s online post and subsequent CJP initiative begin circulating. Media reports the launch; no claim of formal electoral-party registration is made.

events.title: Founder gives early public interview
events.assessment: ThePrint profiles the satirical initiative and Dipke’s stated concern that younger citizens feel disconnected from politics.

events.title: Dipke answers questions in India Today interview
events.assessment: In an on-camera interview, the founder explains his objection to remarks attributed to the Chief Justice, youth frustration and intended peaceful protest. The unedited judicial hearing is a separate source requirement.

events.title: Platform and website restrictions contested
events.assessment: Indian Express examines withheld accounts, website access restrictions and CJP’s changing public identity. Attribution and legal rationale require original orders.

events.title: CJP public press conference aired
events.assessment: ThePrint published a recording labelled as CJP's New Delhi press conference concerning the proposed 6 June protest. Specific claims from the recording remain excluded until reviewed against a time-coded transcript.

events.title: First reported Jantar Mantar mobilisation
events.assessment: Students, exam aspirants and CJP supporters gather in Delhi; organisers demand accountability for examination failures.

events.title: Periodic sit-ins and digital campaigning
events.assessment: The movement shifts from online satire to repeated public organising. The available chronology is a press reconstruction, not a complete daily attendance log.

events.title: Extended Jantar Mantar sit-in begins
events.assessment: Reported return for a sustained sit-in over examinations and ministerial accountability.

events.title: Call to NEET aspirants
events.assessment: Dipke appeals to exam aspirants to join the agitation after their examination obligations.

events.title: Protest maintained, early attendance reported
events.assessment: Coverage describes persistent but still limited physical turnout. Crowd figures are press estimates and not audited totals.

events.title: Sonam Wangchuk begins hunger strike
events.assessment: Wangchuk joins demonstrators with students associated with AISA. His involvement is documented support, not proof of a single organisation controlling all participants.

events.title: Invitation extended across political parties
events.assessment: ThePrint quotes Dipke inviting all parties while rejecting electoral ambitions. A public invitation is distinct from a formal party alliance.

events.title: Opposition and civil-society solidarity grows
events.assessment: Public figures visit or endorse parts of the agitation; formal organisational support varies among parties.

events.title: Congress organisational position examined
events.assessment: ThePrint reports Congress figures expressing solidarity while the party withheld a formal movement endorsement at that point.

events.title: Wangchuk moved to hospital
events.assessment: Police intervention at the protest site and Wangchuk’s hospital transfer are reported; Dipke says he will continue the fast.

events.title: Large turnout before parliament march
events.assessment: Crowds begin gathering for the planned Sansad Chalo mobilisation the following day. Estimates remain source-dependent.

events.title: Sansad Chalo march and clashes
events.assessment: CJP-linked march, public-order operations, injuries and reported clashes. Police and protesters offer competing accounts; casualty and turnout figures are not independently reconciled.

events.title: CJP representatives meet J P Nadda
events.assessment: Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka are reported to have met the Union minister during the protest. This is a public negotiating contact.

events.title: Government talks and shifting protest demands
events.assessment: The movement presses for the education minister’s resignation, FIR relief and assistance for affected students. Reported talks do not confirm implementation.

events.title: Wangchuk ends extended hunger strike
events.assessment: Coverage reports the end of his fast amid negotiations. The timing should be distinguished from later claims about who secured concessions.

events.title: Ministerial resignation officially accepted
events.assessment: The President’s communique confirms Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation and Pralhad Joshi’s additional Education charge. Whether CJP was the sole or determining cause is a separate causal assessment.

events.title: Ranka and Das detail plans in NDTV interview
events.assessment: Das describes an immediate grassroots agenda; Ranka declines to rule out his own eventual political career and describes the terms he understood from government negotiations. The subsequent written court order controls legal scope.

events.title: Supreme Court gives interim protest-related relief
events.assessment: Reporting describes protection for some students arrested in July demonstrations. The September written order is required for later and broader claims.

events.title: Dipke sets out organisational intentions in Aaj Tak Q&A
events.assessment: The founder publicly discusses protest finance, political-party support, the paper-leak law and a 'response group' rather than immediate electoral entry. Statements remain the speaker's accounts unless separately verified.

events.title: 12-member working team publicly profiled
events.assessment: Indian Express reports the CJP office-bearers after a Maharashtra meeting and records its continued stated intention not to form a registered political party.

events.title: Past AAP associations reported
events.assessment: ThePrint identifies six CJP core members with former AAP ties or public support. Dipke and the AAP spokesperson deny a current organisational link; no command or funding relationship is established.

events.title: Supreme Court records mutual settlement
events.assessment: A dated court order closes July protest FIRs within specified terms and exceptions, orders a compensation framework, and records Saurav Das withdrawing a proposed 5 September march.

events.title: Proposed march withdrawn, per court record
events.assessment: Do not record the march as having occurred merely because older publicity announced it. The 1 September order captures the withdrawal.

events.title: New October mobilisation announced
events.assessment: Saurav Das is reported demanding protests beginning 10 October; alleged plans to arrest organisers are his attributed statement, not an established government plan.

events.title: Public-order restrictions scrutinised
events.assessment: Reports describe a Supreme Court hearing on extensive Delhi travel restrictions before planned CJP demonstrations. Reported judicial remarks must not be overstated as a final liability finding.

events.title: Dipke addresses Loksamvad and outlines October protest
events.assessment: During a public event reported by The Indian Express, Dipke argues that transport restrictions are disproportionate, repeats the 13-crore roll figure and rejects an immediate plan to register a political party.

events.title: Delhi protest restrictions and detentions
events.assessment: Reuters reports large-scale preventive measures, transport disruption and arrests before a CJP-backed rally targeting the CEC. Police figures and protest figures differ.

events.title: Further demonstrations after releases
events.assessment: Reuters reports continued action, court activity and competing accounts of treatment of demonstrators, journalists and lawyers.

events.title: CJP organisers enter disputed protest site
events.assessment: Coverage describes Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das arriving at Jantar Mantar despite restrictions. Participants dispute the police account of their conduct.

events.title: Five-day custody ordered
events.assessment: Reuters and Indian Express report a magistrate ordering custody for Ranka and Das. This is a procedural court action, not a conviction.

events.title: Nagpur press interaction: independence and court allegations
events.assessment: Dipke tells reporters CJP is an independent pressure group, says he had no specific discussion with Rahul Gandhi, disputes policing explanations, and criticises courts without identifying particular party-symbol cases.

events.title: Election-roll dispute remains unresolved
events.assessment: Reuters details allegations of large-scale exclusion and the election authority’s denial of partisan bias. A final-voter disenfranchisement total has not been audited here.

events.title: Delhi CM Gupta publicly alleges CJP–AAP alignment
events.assessment: At a Delhi press conference, Rekha Gupta calls CJP an AAP 'B party'. This is a reported public allegation, not independent evidence of a financing or instruction chain.
